findings.title: Task 4 misses the replay's held schema, so its own replay test fails and duel replays with the new fields fail to parse
findings.claim: Task 4 adds throttleHeld, rcsX and rcsY to the codec and to both checkpoint schemas. It does not add them to the strict held schema in authority/replay.ts, which validates every recorded tick's input.held. Task 4's test records a held frame with rcsX 1, then expects parseEncounterReplay on that replay not to throw. It will throw on an unrecognized key. In production, any duel replay or recording that holds the new fields will fail to parse.
findings.evidence: plan L1137 (Task 4 Files: codec, checkpoint, duelCheckpoint and core only); plan L1192-L1194 (`parseEncounterReplay(duelRules, replay, …)` expected not to throw, and the replay contains '"rcsX":1'); src/renderer/src/authority/replay.ts:L17 (`const held = z.object({ moveX, moveY, interactHeld, face, aim, gunHeld }).strict()`); replay.ts:L22 (tick actions use `z.array(held)`). The spec's list (spec L287-L291) omits it too.
findings.why: Task 4 Step 6 runs tests/helmWire.test.ts with the 'checkpoints' filter, which matches this test, so the task fails as written. Duel replays from a session with the new held fields would also fail to parse.
findings.fix: Add `src/renderer/src/authority/replay.ts:17` to Task 4's Files and Step 4. Extend its held schema with `throttleHeld`, `rcsX` and `rcsY`, each `z.number().int().min(-1).max(1).optional()`, the same edit as duelCheckpoint.ts. Add it to the self-review's §7 list.

findings.title: Task 10 calls takeSteer() on the shadowed ContactRequests inside pump(), which fails tsc
findings.claim: Task 10 Step 4(e) inserts `const steerNow = requests.takeSteer()` into pump(). Inside pump, `requests` is the local `contact.takeRequests()` result, of type ContactRequests, which shadows the session-level MapRequests. ContactRequests has no takeSteer, so `npx tsc -b` fails with TS2339.
findings.evidence: plan L3253 (`const steerNow = requests.takeSteer(), crewHelmSeat = …`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/onlineDuel.ts:L252 (`const k = keyboard.sample(), requests = contact.takeRequests(), heading = requests0();`); onlineDuel.ts:L83 (the outer `requests = createMapRequests()`); onlineDuel.ts:L101 (the existing workaround `requests0 = () => requests.takeHeading()`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/contactController.ts:L28 (ContactRequests: designate, scan, torpStep?, rockLock?, noLaser?); src/renderer/src/app/duel/mapRequests.ts:L10 (takeSteer lives on MapRequests).
findings.why: Task 10 Step 5's `npx tsc -b` fails, and without this the online crew Helm never steers.
findings.fix: Mirror `requests0`. At session scope, beside `requests0`, add `const takeSteer0 = (): number | null => requests.takeSteer();`, and in pump use `const steerNow = takeSteer0()`. Better still, drain it right after `heading = requests0()` on L252, so a steer is never left stale across the early returns on L260 and L268.

findings.title: Task 3 breaks tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts, which hard-codes the helm module as two values, and does not edit it
findings.claim: Task 3 grows the helm module to six values (interiorAt = helmAt + 6). tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts computes the interior offset as `at + 5 + 4 + 2`, then writes bad values at fieldsAt + k and expects /interior sim version/, /interior layout/ and /crew count/. After Task 3, those writes land on thrMille and rcsGas, and the snapshot is refused with 'thrMille 1000000 is invalid' instead. Task 3 Step 8 edits only duelModules.test.ts and duel.test.ts, but Step 9 runs duelSnapshot.test.ts and expects PASS. This failure is not a trajectory pin, so it cannot go into K, and the plan's rule sends the implementer to 'fix the code'.
findings.evidence: plan L1082 (`interiorAt = helmAt + 6`); plan L1111-L1115 (Step 8 edits two test files only); plan L1122 (Step 9 runs tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts); tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts:L109 (`const interiorAt = at + 5 + 4 + 2, fieldsAt = interiorAt;   // … the helm module (Artemis-ii's throttle, Feel-ii's held heading)`); tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts:L115-L117 (the specific regexes). tests/crewOfFourWire.test.ts:L63 hard-codes `+ 4 + 2` too, but its assertions are a bare `toThrow()`, so it still passes.
findings.why: Task 3 cannot reach a green targeted run as written, and the K rule actively misdirects the fix.
findings.fix: Add to Task 3 Step 8: in tests/duelSnapshot.test.ts:109, replace `at + 5 + 4 + 2` with `at + 5 + 4 + 6`, and extend its comment with 'playtest2feedback §7: thrMille, rcsGas, rcsAcc, compressor'. Optionally fix crewOfFourWire.test.ts:63 the same way, so it keeps testing what it says it does. Add both files to the commit.

findings.title: Task 5 Step 8's file list is incomplete, and duelOnlineView's throttle test breaks in Task 10, which has no migration rule
findings.claim: Step 8 names eight files and says 'Apply these edits, and nothing else'. The same grep also matches tests/duelInputMerge.test.ts, tests/duelOnlineView.test.ts and tests/duelRuntime.test.ts. duelRuntime's throttle asserts (L614, L630) fail in Task 5, and Step 9's catch-all handles them. duelOnlineView.test.ts:L189-L199 ('the Helm seat flies the replica throttle') still passes in Task 5. Task 10 then changes onlineSource.axes() to crewAxes on the Cutter, and that test fails in Task 10 Step 5's run. Task 10 gives no rule to move it to the Valkyrn, and the global rule says to fix the code.
findings.evidence: plan L1717-L1719 (the grep and its claimed eight-file listing); grep of tests for `kind: 'throttle'|throttle(`: duelInputMerge.test.ts (4), duelOnlineView.test.ts (4), duelRuntime.test.ts (3), all missing from L1719; tests/duelOnlineView.test.ts:L195 (`expect([source.axes(), source.throttle()]).toEqual([{ turn: 1, thrust: 0.5 }, 2])`); plan L3151 (online axes become crewAxes); plan L3276 (Task 10 runs duelOnlineView.test.ts and expects PASS).
findings.why: Anything the implementer has to guess is a defect, and here the stated rule points the wrong way.
findings.fix: Correct the Step 8 listing to eleven files. State that duelInputMerge's keyboard-only tests need no edit. Move duelRuntime's throttle `it`s to `createDuelRuntime({ …, cls: ShipClass.Valkyrn })` and duelOnlineView's L189 `it` to a Valkyrn replica now. Or add to Task 10 Step 5 an explicit Decision 17 migration for any online-source test of the notched throttle.

findings.title: The known-red list K can miss crew-trajectory pins and can mask new failures
findings.claim: K is recorded only from the globs in Task 2 Step 10, Task 5 Step 9 and Task 7 Step 8. Task 8's closing run uses globs too, and the first full suite runs in Task 13, after K is closed. Several test files step a Cutter duel or the runtime and match none of these globs: ftlTargeting, ownShipScene, contactScene, shipHudScene, interiorZoomScene and commandUnion. A trajectory pin in one of them first fails in Task 13, which has no rule for it. Also, once a test is in K, later tasks never check that it still fails only on its pinned number. A new exception or a NaN in a K test stays hidden until Task 8.
findings.evidence: plan L19 (the K rule); plan L651, L1740, L2331 (the recording globs: duel*, feel*, tactical*, online*, sci*, science*, hunter*, rock*, spike*, asteroid*); plan L2476 (Task 8's closing globs, adding valkyrn*, crew*, helm*); plan L3991 (the first full suite, Task 13); grep of tests for stepDuelTick, scriptedInput or createDuelRuntime: ftlTargeting.test.ts, ownShipScene.test.ts, contactScene.test.ts, shipHudScene.test.ts, interiorZoomScene.test.ts and commandUnion.test.ts are outside every glob.
findings.why: A real regression from Tasks 2 to 7 could be re-pinned as a moved number, or surface only at the end with no defined handling.
findings.fix: Run `npx electron-vite build` and the full suite in Task 2 Step 10, and again at the end of Task 8 after the re-pin, with K's admission rule. In Tasks 5 and 7, re-run each K test and confirm it fails on the same assertion with only the pinned number moved. Anything else is a bug in that task.

findings.title: If the Task 8 gate cannot be tuned, the whole plan stops, though Tasks 9-13 do not depend on it
findings.claim: Task 8 says that if no knob setting holds the gate, the implementer stops and reports. Tasks 9 to 13 (client, UI, puffs, bless) do not need the gate, and the spike's acceptance is the owner's playtest. The scripted crew also never sends helmPower, so it flies the whole duel at cap 750 (3 + 1). With no drag and a 2.4 s ramp, that makes its bang-bang orbit harder to tune, and the knob list cannot change it.
findings.evidence: plan L2447 ('If no setting inside these bounds holds, stop and report the closest summary'); plan L2438-L2446 (the knobs: orbit, slack, evade, avoid, missile gap, MAX_SPEED); plan L1690-L1696 (the scripted crew holds only throttleHeld); spec L232 (round start compressor min(1, HELM_BARS)); spec L390-L391 (the gates are tuned until they pass).
findings.why: A tuning miss would block delivery of the playable branch for the owner's playtest.
findings.fix: Add a knob 0: the scripted crew sends one `helmPower +1` on its first seated tick, for cap 1000. That is a scripted-pair choice, not a rule change. And if the gate still fails, record the closest summary in the Task 8 commit, mark the scripted-pair gate as an owner-visible known failure, and continue with Tasks 9 to 13.

findings.title: The crew HelmStation's bottom rows sit lower than the existing block's and may clip the 200 px panel
findings.claim: With FONT_NATIVE at 16 px, the gauge's rate text sits at y = barTop + BAR_H + 16 = 698, and the last hint line at y0 + 182 = 696. The panel ends at 708. The existing block's lowest row is at y0 + 170 = 684.
findings.evidence: plan L3501-L3502 and L3517; src/renderer/src/render/theme.ts:L22 (FONT_NATIVE = 16); src/renderer/src/render/duel/consoleLayout.ts:L10-L11 (STATION.h.helm 200, stationTop = 720 − 12 − 200); src/renderer/src/ui/duel/HelmStation.tsx:L70 (the lowest existing row at y0 + 170).
findings.why: This is a cosmetic risk at the owner's look gate.
findings.fix: Move the three hint rows up 12 px (y0 + 138, 154, 170), and put `+rate%/S` beside the percentage rather than below it. Or check it in the Task 13 screenshot.

verified: Drag ships fly bit-identically: today's ax is ((0 + g) + e) + t; the new drag path is ((0 + g) + e) + (0 + t), and 0 + t = t. Reverse r = 1 multiplies exactly, and gx + (0 − p) equals gx − p. turn × 1 × tsp × f is unchanged, and idle is unchanged with rcs absent. Whole levels (−1, ¼, ½, ¾, 1) round to thousandths exactly. The Hunter only sends −1, 0 and 1 (hunter.ts:L95-L105). Task 2's flyShipToday test covers every class, Engines level and Valkyrn level (physics.ts:L29-L59, plan L192-L247).
Crew thrust loses nothing to the thousandths rounding: crewThrust(m) = m/1000 or 4m/1000 for integer m, so the rounding is exact. The cap follows spec §2's four steps (plan L503-L510).

Integer gas: compress at 50, 100 and 150 sixtieths gives exactly 1200, 600 and 400 ticks. compress(990, 50, 3) is {993, 20}. The ramp and return pins hold: 994/1000 at 142/143 ticks, −245/−250 at 35/36, and 966, 14 then 0 on release (plan L780-L809).

Boost far bands: a boosted step is at most floor(acc + 3.56) ≤ 4 whole indices. From |d| ≥ 5 it lands at |d| ≥ 1, and from beyond 4.27 indices (sin 6°) it stays outside AUTO_FACE_SIN (sin 2.5°). It never crosses. BOOST_FACE_SIN = 0.10452846326765347 is sin 6° (hunter.ts:L42-L48, tuning AUTO_FACE_SIN L127).

Bless guard: Task 1's bump alone passes blessRefusal through both proofs (one version step). Task 13's same-version bless returns undefined without calling the proofs (scripts/golden/blessGuard.ts:L22-L36, scripts/bless-golden.ts:L41).
